name: MN-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Omar's incumbency and large fundraising edge
Markets price Omar at ~96% to win
model.rationale: The D+32 district fundamentals, Omar's incumbency and roughly eight-to-one fundraising advantage, and Polymarket pricing near 96% all point to an easy Democratic hold, so the forecast stays near the baseline with modest tightening for the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much narrower margin or a surge of outside spending against Omar would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minneapolis-based MN-05 is one of the most Democratic-leaning House districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+32. Incumbent Ilhan Omar is seeking another term after easily securing renomination, and she enters the general election with a large financial edge: about $5.8 million raised and $1.3 million on hand, versus roughly $747,000 raised and under $50,000 on hand for Republican John Nagel. No outside groups are active in the race.

With no public general-election polling, the outlook rests on district fundamentals, which point to a Democratic margin near thirty points. Prediction markets price Omar's chances at about 96 percent. The seat is rated Safe D, with only minor residual uncertainty from the lack of polling.
